title: Duke of Sessa to Charles V, Rome, 18 April 1524, RAH Salazar A-31 (9/31) ff. 128-131 (DECODE R9877-R9878)

documents.shelfmark: RAH Colección Salazar y Castro A-31 (9/31) ff. 128-131 (DECODE R9877, R9878 duplicate)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the letter or its duplicate; Bergenroth's CSP Spain vol. 2 skips it. Sibling letters in the same cipher carry the court's decipherments (ff. 140, 172, 324).

transcription.source: DECODE images (R9877, R9878), cut into token tiles by tokens.py
transcription.notes: Nine cipher lines (eight on f. 128r, one on f. 128v); the duplicate ff. 130-131 is token-for-token the same. The transcription file mixes two passes and clear text, so it cannot be measured as it stands.

documents.shelfmark: RAH Colección Salazar y Castro A-31 (9/31) ff. 79-86 (DECODE R9873)

plaintext.source: No decipherment bound with it. CSP Spain ii 637 cites Goicoechea's 19th-c. deciphering (not imaged); no. 636 abstracts the triplicate's contemporary deciphering (Gayangos MS), no. 638 a court abstract. The English abstracts served as a topic crib only.

transcription.source: DECODE images in img/ (git-ignored), read in strips with a crop script
transcription.notes: Cipher runs on ff. 80v-84r and the postscript f. 86r; ff. 79r-80r, 84v-85v clear. Token count = the (a) lines of r9873_cipher.txt (--skip non-(a)/(c) lines --drop-first), so it includes f~ switches, v db openers and the few clear words quoted inside cipher lines. Read as sense (measure_read.py): 92.8% with pass-17 tentative values, 87.8% strict.

documents.shelfmark: RAH Colección Salazar y Castro A-34 (9/34) ff. 150-156 (DECODE R9898)

plaintext.source: Six cipher runs carry a contemporary marginal decipherment in a second hand (ff. 150r, 152r, 153v, 154r, 154v x3, 156r); the rest has none. Not calendared in CSP Spain iii.1.

transcription.source: DECODE images in img/ (git-ignored), read in strips with a crop script
transcription.notes: Clear and cipher interleaved throughout; heavy bleed-through on ff. 150v-151r and 155v. Token count as for r9873 (includes f~ and quoted clear words). Read as sense (measure_read.py): 79.8% with pass-17 tentative values, 77.9% strict.

system.summary: Mixed nomenclator: three-letter code groups for words, names and syllables plus single letters and signs for spelling, with a clear/cipher switch sign and a null paragraph opener.
system.sibling_key: Same cipher as Sessa's decrypted despatches of 1523-25 (ff. 138/140, 168-172, 322-324; R9897, R9893, R9834 and others); the key was rebuilt from them.
system.notes: About 110 code groups and the letter alphabet recovered (README). Homophones: several code variants (no ler/lex, con tat/tar). f~ switches clear/cipher; 'v db' is a null opener.

prior_solution.where: DECODE lists it Non-decrypted; not in CSP Spain; only sibling letters carry decipherments

conditions.human_role: Downloaded DECODE images logged in and supplied the DECODE cookie

solution.what: Identified DECODE's '1424' as 1524, the Duke of Sessa, Salazar A-31, and located the decrypted siblings in CSP Spain vol. 2.
Cut every cipher line of f. 128 and the siblings into token tiles; collated the duplicate f. 130.
Passes 1-9: aligned sibling ciphers (ff. 138, 168v, 170-171, 322) against their clears to assign code and letter values.
Passes 10-13: 1525 and July 1524 siblings (R9897, R9898, R9893) settled rad, lif, hud, zum and others.
Pass 14: template matching over the seven 1523 decrypted letters gave z y = -on; vo, per, ruc, hay remain unattested.
Word-level reading of the nine cipher lines, with four groups and one clause open.

Retry of the open groups (vo, per, ruc, hay, m-re clause) with the pass-15 key over the new full R9660 transcription; ruc gets five contexts (a verb/adjective root), none fixes a value; vo/per absent.
Took CSP Spain ii 636-638 (the 14 Apr 1524 despatch, its triplicate and the court abstract) from the BHO copy in targets/sanchez1523/csp; checked CSP iii.1 (BHO) for R9898: not calendared.
Transcribed every cipher run of R9873 (ff. 80v-86r) and R9898 (ff. 150r-156r) from the DECODE images in two-line strips into the (a)/(b) convention, appending page by page.
Found that R9898 is not without decipherment, as pass 12 had concluded: six cipher runs have a marginal decipherment in a second hand.
Aligned the six R9898 marginal decipherments: v em = cierto, li = mi, le = me, net = halla (not toma), lec = -mos, yol = aqui, sud = datario, Jac = obliga-, cap = tem-, nuh = grande.

Used CSP 636's English abstract as a topic crib for R9873: fed = rey de Francia (the pension; 'send a person under honest colour'), xir = cardenal, lot = nuncio, pof = exercito; values taken only where a second Spanish context agreed.

Cross-letter context: ruc/rus = dicho (pair of rad = dicha; 'el dicho datario', 'los dichos quatro mill ducados'), cuq = tengo, tig = contra, kuc = liga, yod/quf = amigo/enemigo, and the name Micer Agostino Foyeta; hay = aunque (tentative).
Read both letters with the pass-16 key; measured with measure_read.py (assembled words scored on es-golden-age): R9873 2165/2473 tokens (87.5%), R9898 2361/3059 (77.2%).
Retried the f. 128 residue with the new values: rus = dicho and hay = aunque give 'de lo susodicho, aunque no, me parece que concuerda'; vo and per occur in neither letter; the m-re clause unchanged.
About 260 code groups across the two letters (most attested once) and 398 letter tokens on the bleed-through pages of R9898 stay unread.

Pass 17: pooled the open groups of R9873, R9898 and R9660 into one concordance (84 groups in two or more letters) and took values that read in every occurrence (cas tiene, var agora, rac dize, pam/Jir paga, xoc socorr-, leg mucho, sur/luc parte, len/lon buen-, 3ar aca, yer Florencia, gig quisie-, nuf gente and ~15 single-context ones); all tentative.
Tested alphabetical bracketing of the code: attested values do not follow code order (cad sobre, cas tiene, cap tem-, cot todo), so no bracketing.
Re-cut R9873's non-word spellings and R9898 ff. 150v-151r at 1.5-1.6x: one correction (f. 83r p-u-e-r-e = pudiesse); the rest stand as written; bleed-through on R9898 does not resolve.
Looked for a better image of R9898 on the RAH Biblioteca Digital (search behind a bot wall; web search finds no digitised Salazar A-34).
Re-measured: R9873 92.8% (strict 87.8%), R9898 79.8% (strict 77.9%); the 95% target was not reached.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The code values were rebuilt by aligning deciphered sibling letters in the same RAH Salazar A-31 volume (ff. 138/140, 170-172, 322-324, R9893 f. 483/485) and other Sessa letters of 1523-25 with their contemporary clears; the rebuilt key was then applied to ff. 128-131.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription_f128.txt pass-2 lines P1-P8: 116 cipher tokens; after pass 16 rus (= dicho) and hay (= aunque, tentative) read, so 104/116; open: vo, per and the m-re clause plus the end 'r-[...]' (~10). Sibling letters measured separately (read_r9873.md 87.5%, read_r9898.md 77.2%).
outcome.notes: Residue of f. 128 after pass 16: vo, per, the clause 'los m-re que r-ido'; hay = aunque tentative. R9873 (14 Apr 1524) and R9898 (24 Feb 1525) transcribed and read in part in the same key (pass 16); R9898's marginal decipherments (missed in pass 12) supplied about 15 values. Pass 17 (3 Oct): pooled open groups across R9873/R9898/R9660; R9873 92.8% (strict 87.8%), R9898 79.8% (strict 77.9%); 95% not reached.
